acceptanceCriteria: Decision recorded: qualify the store state dir instead of the Git common dir, or keep the common dir with a stated reason, with the TM-V0-010 text updated to match.

If changed: with only <common>/taskman writable (e.g. a Codex workspace-write sandbox), a claim succeeds. A test proves the probe is created under the store state dir and never in the common dir root.
docs/TASKS-SUPERVISION.md writable-root guidance updated to the narrowest root that works.
body:
Observed 2026-10-01 while qualifying a Codex host for `corvint-tasks dispatch` (V1-0475; PR stacked on beamfall/corvint#436).

Every store mutation calls `authority.Qualify(repo.CommonDir)` (internal/tasks/store/*.go). That writes an O_EXCL probe `.taskman-qualify-<pid>-<random>.tmp` directly in the Git common dir (internal/tasks/authority/qualify.go:45), while the journal lives in `<common>/taskman`. A sandboxed worker host therefore cannot grant only the store's state directory.

Reproduction (codex-cli 0.153.2, macOS):
- run `codex exec --sandbox workspace-write -c 'sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots=["<repo>/.git/taskman"]'`;
- have the worker run `corvint-tasks ticket claim`.

Expected: the claim succeeds, because the store's own state directory is writable.

Actual: the claim fails UNSUPPORTED_FILESYSTEM, because the probe in `<repo>/.git` is refused. It succeeds only when all of `<repo>/.git` is writable. That root also lets the worker write refs and objects, which widens what an operator must grant to a sandboxed agent.

Idea: qualify (and probe in) the directory that actually holds the store state, `<common>/taskman`, creating it first if TM-V0-010 allows. Alternatively, document why the common-dir root is required. This changes the TM-V0-010 qualification root, so it needs a spec amendment.
title: Tasks store: qualify the taskman state dir so sandboxed hosts need not write the whole Git common dir
